articles.title: SpaceX proposes more than $74 billion for two AI supercomputing campuses
articles.dek: SpaceX says it plans to put more than $24 billion into Starbase, Texas and roughly $50 billion into Cochise County, Arizona. This is proposed spending from a company statement — not money spent or built yet — and both sites still need local decisions on Dec. 9.
articles.image_alt: Editorial illustration of desert AI supercomputing campuses with circuit-patterned data center buildings, cooling towers, power lines and a rocket on a launch pad at sunrise
articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow. Two desert campuses, one very large proposal — and two local votes still to come on Dec. 9.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: Proposed total:
More than $74 billion across two AI supercomputing campuses, according to a SpaceX statement reported by Reuters.
Split:
More than $24 billion at Starbase, Texas and roughly $50 billion in Cochise County, Arizona.
Not yet built:
This is proposed spending, not money spent or construction completed, and both sites still need local decisions on Dec. 9.
Dec. 9 decisions:
A Cochise County zoning hearing and a Starbase tax-abatement vote.

articles.title: The drone war arrived before America was ready for it
articles.dek: Iran's thousands of cheap one-way drones overwhelmed defenses built for a different kind of war, and Ukraine's drone arithmetic exposed how far behind the United States had fallen on scale, cost, and speed. The Pentagon's reorganization is real; whether it closes the gap before the next test is the open question.
articles.image_alt: Editorial illustration of a formation of small drones flying over the sea toward warships, with a radar plane overhead and a radar station on a desert shore at sunset
articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: estimated Shahed-family drones Iran launched between Feb. 28 and early April, with 2,210 aimed at the UAE alone.
The gap:
cheap first-person-view drones against exquisite systems. The U.S. had zero FPV attack drones in October 2025; the Marines had fielded 3,500 by May 2026.
The response:
a $1 billion Drone Dominance plan for more than 200,000 FPV drones by 2027, and a new Autonomous Warfare Command standing up Oct. 1, 2027.
Next test:
the Pacific, where thousands of unmanned systems would operate at once and radar planes would be hunted.

articles.title: The U.S. closed the last big loophole in its AI chip ban — by going after the landlords
articles.dek: A rule that took effect today forces cloud operators to prove their compute isn't reaching China, and puts new license requirements on advanced GPUs headed to five countries.
articles.image_alt: Editorial illustration of a data center hall with glowing GPU server racks, a world map highlighting countries in Southeast Asia and South America, and a padlock over the racks
articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow. The rule follows the compute, not just the chips.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The rule:
Published Nov 19 and effective immediately — an interim final rule from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security.
Two controls:
A worldwide remote-access control keyed to 12 million aggregate TPP, and a license requirement for most advanced-GPU transfers to or within Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil.
Who's excepted:
U.S.-headquartered companies can use the five-country exception only by filing monthly reports with BIS.
What's not covered:
Infrastructure used only for commercial recommender systems is exempt; the rule also rescinds most of the Biden-era AI Diffusion Framework.

articles.title: Jensen Huang wants his job back. The board — and the betting markets — say not so fast
articles.dek: Nvidia's board said it does not intend to reinstate its ousted founder. Traders put his chances of being named CEO again at about 1 in 10, and his chances of any formal Nvidia role by the end of 2027 at about 3 in 10.
articles.image_alt: Editorial illustration of an empty leather executive chair at the head of a boardroom table at dusk, with a city skyline through floor-to-ceiling windows
articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow. The chair is empty, and the board says it intends to keep it that way.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The offer:
On Nov 17 Huang said he would be 'honored' to return as CEO if the board decides it is in the company's best interest.
The answer:
Hours later, board chair Harvey Jones said the board 'does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.'
The odds:
Kalshi gives him about a 9% chance of the CEO job, with Rene Haas leading at about 29%; Polymarket gives him about 30% of holding any formal Nvidia role by the end of 2027.
What's next:
Huang testifies behind closed doors before House committees on Dec 1 about chip smuggling and export control evasion; general counsel Tim Teter follows on Dec 2.

articles.dek: The maker of Claude raised more in its initial offering than any company before it, and it has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments to pay for.

articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow. The biggest IPO in history — and a $900 billion compute bill behind it.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The price:
$83 a share, above the $70–$78 marketed range.
The raise:
980 million shares sold for $81.3 billion — the largest initial IPO raise on record. SpaceX's total later reached $86.2 billion after its overallotment.
The valuation:
Roughly $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion fully diluted, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT — and about $2 trillion at Thursday's open.
The catch:
About $900 billion in future compute commitments, and a $104 billion net loss in the first nine months — mostly an accounting charge on convertible notes, not cash.

articles.title: An Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped him prove the Riemann Hypothesis. The proof is 250,000 pages long.
articles.dek: Levent Alpöge says he worked with Claude for six weeks to produce a proof of the 167-year-old problem. One Oxford mathematician says he's '98 or 99 percent certain' it's right — but nobody has verified it yet.
articles.image_alt: Editorial illustration of a chalkboard covered in prime number spirals and equations, a glowing AI chat window, and a towering stack of paper
articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow. A 250,000-page proof, written with an AI's help.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The claim:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he worked with Claude for six weeks to build a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, written up in Lean and running to more than 250,000 pages.
The prize:
The Clay Mathematics Institute offers $1 million for the first correct solution of the 167-year-old problem, proposed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859.
The caveat:
The proof has not been verified, and checking it will take time. Oxford mathematician James Maynard says he is '98 or 99 percent certain' it is accurate — his assessment, not a confirmation.
The question:
It is unclear whether Claude was essential to the breakthrough, or a powerful tool in a mathematician's hands.

articles.title: Signal is blocking screenshots on your phone, because your operating system's AI can read them
articles.dek: The messaging app is extending its screenshot block from Windows to Android and iOS. Its president calls OS-level AI agents an 'existential threat' — and admits the fix is incomplete.
articles.image_alt: Editorial illustration of a smartphone with a private messaging conversation, a padlock over the screen, and an AI eye blocked by a shield
articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow. Signal can lock its own app — but not the operating system around it.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The change:
Signal is blocking screenshots in its Android and iOS apps, after already doing so on Windows, because OS-level AI agents can scan what is on screen.
The reason:
President Meredith Whittaker calls operating systems that integrate agentic AI an 'existential threat' to private messaging.
The limit:
Users can turn the block off, which Whittaker says would 'break our privacy guarantees.'
The gap:
Whittaker admits the block is 'incomplete' — it does not stop sneakier ways AI agents could reach app data.

articles.title: Meta is "re-evaluating" its 2030 net-zero goal as AI data centers push its emissions up nearly 40%
articles.dek: The company's carbon footprint jumped from 15.6 million to more than 21.7 million metric tonnes in a year — the biggest percentage rise of any Big Tech giant.
articles.image_alt: Editorial illustration of a data center with glowing server halls and smoking cooling towers, a tipping net-zero gauge, and a rising emissions chart
articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow. The AI buildout is pushing Meta's emissions up, not down.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The rethink:
Meta's 2026 sustainability report, published Nov 19, says the company is 're-evaluating' its 2030 net-zero goal and near-term targets.
The numbers:
Total emissions rose from 15.6 million to more than 21.7 million metric tonnes in a year — nearly 40% — and net emissions rose 45%, to more than 11.8 million tonnes.
The comparison:
Microsoft's footprint rose 25%, Google's 18% and Amazon's 16%; all three have stuck by their original goals so far.
The water:
Facility water use fell to 790 million gallons, but use in water-stressed areas rose to 246 million, and power-generation water use topped 26 billion gallons.

sources: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers — Ars Technica

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The recalls:
Two software recalls across Waymo's fleet of 3,871 robotaxis.
The fixes:
The cars will stop entering closed highway construction zones and respond better to police and emergency crews directing traffic.
The trigger:
Several incidents involving construction breaches and ignored officer signals.
The consequence:
California banned Waymo from freeways, forcing a nationwide pause on highway operations.

briefs.title: Agile Robots closes a $500M Series F
briefs.body: Agile Robots closed a $500 million Series F led by SoftBank at an $8.5 billion valuation. Nvidia, Hitachi and T.Capital also took part, bringing the company’s total funding to about $2 billion.

briefs.title: Griffin raises $20M to add cards and stablecoin services
briefs.body: Griffin, a UK licensed bank for fintechs, raised $20 million in a Series B announced Nov. 12, led by Octagon Partners with Notion Capital, A+ Ventures, Nordic Ninja and Breega taking part, at a valuation above $100 million. The plan is to expand into card issuing — branded retail and corporate debit cards, with credit to follow — and stablecoin services, including reserve services for stablecoin businesses and on-chain cross-border payments. Those are planned services, not launched, and no rollout schedule was given.

briefs.title: Anthropic opens a private beta for self-hosted Claude Managed Agents
briefs.body: Anthropic opened a private beta on Nov. 12 that lets companies run the Claude Managed Agents service — the harness, sandboxes, credentials and session history — in their own cloud or on-premises. The model itself does not move: model requests still go to Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google’s Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or the customer’s own gateway. Access is by request through an Anthropic account team, with no pricing or general-availability date given. This is a private beta only — not a general release and not a fully offline Claude. The same day, Anthropic launched Claude for Manufacturing for Team and Enterprise plans, with 17 skills and connectors for Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365 and Oracle NetSuite.

briefs.title: UFORCE raises $700M to build Ukraine's drone arsenal at scale
briefs.body: UFORCE, the London-headquartered, Ukrainian-founded maker of uncrewed sea, air, and land systems, raised a $700 million Series A at a $6 billion valuation on November 12, co-led by Valor Equity Partners and the UK National Wealth Fund, which put in £113 million (about $150 million) — the fund's largest defense investment to date — with the U.S.–Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund also taking part. The company says its MAGURA sea drones contributed to the destruction of more than a dozen Russian warships, and its NEMESIS strike drones have flown more than 300,000 combat flights; those figures are the company's own and have not been independently verified. No revenue was disclosed.

briefs.title: Microsoft's Ignite brings specialist AI models for coding, security, and small decisions
briefs.body: At Ignite, Microsoft announced MAI Code 2 for agentic coding, MAI Cyber 2 Flash with 12 billion active parameters for cybersecurity, and Microsoft-Decision-1.1 for routing, classification, and verification tasks too small for a large general model. It also introduced Agent 365 Business Analytics to tie AI spending to business outcomes. Separately, Microsoft said on November 13 it will switch the small language model built into Windows from Phi Silica to the 2.3-billion-parameter Aion Instruct.

briefs.title: After a week of outages, a bipartisan bill would create a board to investigate AI and cyber failures
briefs.body: Reps. Morgan Luttrell (R-Texas) and Ritchie Torres (D-N.Y.) introduced the ROOT CAUSE Act on Wednesday to establish a National Cyber and AI Investigations Board inside CISA, to determine why significant incidents happened and recommend ways to prevent them from recurring. The bill follows a nationwide FAA ground stop that delayed more than 10,000 flights, a Microsoft outage that disrupted workplace tools, and an outage on the NSA's classified NSANet network. A companion proposal, the AI INSIGHT Act from Rep. Matt Van Epps, would direct CISA to help agencies identify AI agents on federal networks and limit their access.

briefs.title: WIRED: the Nvidia board's problem with Huang was his 'lack of candor'
briefs.body: WIRED reports, citing sources, that the Nvidia board's main issue ahead of Jensen Huang's resignation was the former chief executive's 'lack of candor' — amid allegations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report and an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. The board said on November 17 it 'does not intend' to reinstate Huang as CEO.

briefs.title: An AI debt-collection service exposed 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings
briefs.body: Two serious vulnerabilities in CreditNirvana, an AI debt-collection platform, would have let attackers access 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings — along with emails, texts and credit reports. The bugs were patched in June and disclosed in October.

briefs.title: After a week of talks, the UN agrees to two more years of talking about 'killer robots'
briefs.body: After a week of negotiations in Geneva that ran until 4:30 a.m. on Saturday, 128 countries agreed to spend two years 'elaborating' on a possible accord on lethal autonomous weapons — not 'negotiating' one, a word several countries rejected. About 100 countries had pushed for swift, legally binding rules; the United States, Russia and Israel opposed them. The International Committee of the Red Cross, which wanted binding rules within a year, said it regretted the outcome, and the Stop Killer Robots coalition called the mandate 'watered down.'
